audit.whatIsWrong: Four places claim 'his Q silence cancels your Pop Blossom channel mid-wind-up' (whys[4], spikes[1].text, wants.foe[1], content.mid). Null Sphere has no silence — Riot's text says it damages and interrupts channels, and the kit carries no silence flag.
audit.why: The mirror audit verified this on the wiki: Null Sphere has no silence, and _missing-interactions' entry here is inverted (Null Sphere interrupts channels, it is not one). The real level-6 interaction is simpler and true: Riftwalk is a blink at 500 range and roots do not stop blinks, so a landed Tangle-Barbs no longer holds him for the follow-up.
audit.corrected: whys[4], spikes[1].text, wants.foe[1] and content.mid now state the blink-versus-root fact instead of the silence.
sources: kit: Kassadin Q text and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns treats Riftwalk as something to wait out ('read it like a second minimap') with no numbers, and the page gives no sequencing cues at all (packet: sequencingCues 0).
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2 seconds. There is no downtime to commit into after 6 — that is exactly why every kill has to come before it, and why the level-6 row is the hinge. The spikes that matter are level 3 (E into Q re-bloom on a blinkless melee) and level 6 against Neeko.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries Riftwalk's 5s-to-2s clock, Tangle-Barbs' 12s, and the knock-up-not-root distinction.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.diff says HARD while diffRating reads 4/10 and both rating lines say 'Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10' — against a 14.29% win rate over 14 games.
audit.why: The page contradicts itself: the verdict field and the numbers next to it disagree, and the win rate agrees with the verdict, not the numbers. Mechanically Kassadin's Void Stone reduces magic damage and Null Sphere shields against magic — Neeko's entire kit is magic — and he out-scales her outright.
audit.corrected: diffRating 4/10 to 7/10, carryRating 5/10 to 8/10, and both 'Favoured matchup' lines to 'Hard matchup'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page tells the Neeko player that Kassadin's two passives blunt her damage type specifically.
audit.why: Void Stone reduces magic damage taken and Null Sphere's excess energy shields against magic. Neeko deals no physical damage at all, so both apply to every spell she casts — it changes the all-in maths at every stage.
audit.corrected: report[5].t now states it alongside the blink fact.
sources: kit: Kassadin Q text and shield flag

I don't chase a blinking Kassadin — I crash waves, deny his XP, and try to convert my early lead or get him camped before his Tear and Rod of Ages come online.
